chip-blocks.title: Inside the SFM flow meter
chip-blocks.alt: Block diagram of the SFM flow meter: its function blocks, how they connect and which package pins reach each block.
chip-blocks.description: The SFM flow meter's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches.

chip-capabilities.title: What the SFM flow meter does
chip-capabilities.alt: Capability map of the SFM flow meter: Flow measurement (supported): Starts continuous measurement and reads each CRC-checked sample as a flow in millilitres per minute; Gas and gas mixture (supported): Picks the calibrated gas or an oxygen mixture, and changes the mixture without stopping the sensor; Temperature (supported): Reads the sensor temperature from the sample where the part sends it, or by a pointer sequence; Averaging (supported): Averages until the read, or over a fixed number of the 2 kHz measurements; Scale factor and offset (supported): Reads the sensor's scale factor, offset and unit and checks them against the datasheet table; Product identification (supported): Reads the product identifier or serial number and matches it to one of the 32 variants; Sleep and reset (supported): Stops the measurement, sleeps and wakes the sensor, and resets it by command, reset pin or supply cycle; Status and fault checks (supported): Checks each sample's status word and range, and reports a reset, a stale value or a CRC error; Result-ready line (not covered): IRQn goes low when a reading is ready; the driver polls over I2C and leaves the pin open.
chip-capabilities.description: Each card is one function of the SFM flow meter: an icon, its name and what it does for the application. The filled pill says how this driver covers it (legend below); the outlined pills are the chip registers behind it. The coverage table in the README gives the driver calls and the datasheet section of each card.

chip-circuit-address.title: SFM flow meter: Address selection
chip-circuit-address.alt: Schematic of the SFM flow meter address selection: the chip with R3 resistor 2.7 kΩ.
chip-circuit-address.description: A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected.

chip-hero.title: SFM flow meter
chip-hero.alt: Overview of the SFM flow meter, a family of digital gas mass flow sensors on I2C: each part reports the flow of its calibrated gases and gas mixtures and its own temperature as 16-bit words, and the reference SFM4300 does so for air, oxygen, nitrous oxide and carbon dioxide. A MCU talks to it over I2C; it reads back Gas flow, Sensor temperature. Headline figures: 20 or 50 slm SFM4300 flow range; 3.0 to 5.5 V SFM4300 supply; 1 MHz I2C clock at most; 2 kHz flow update rate, no averaging.
chip-hero.description: The SFM flow meter in the middle, drawn as its JST NSH 6-pin connector package. On the left the MCU that runs the driver, joined to it by I2C. Below it, what the chip reads back. The tiles at the bottom are the headline numbers, each with the datasheet section and page it comes from.

driver-layers.title: The layers, one of them yours
driver-layers.alt: Layer diagram: your application calls the SfmFlowMeter core, which sends register reads and writes through the I2C port contract to the port class you write, which drives the chip; the core and the contract are the same on every MCU.
driver-layers.description: Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.

driver-states.title: Driver states
driver-states.alt: State machine of the SFM driver with the states Uninitialized, Idle, Measuring, Asleep and StateUnknown, and the calls that move it between them.
driver-states.description: Five states. The driver starts Uninitialized and EnsureInitialized moves it to Idle. In Idle, StartMeasurement leads to Measuring and Sleep leads to Asleep; WakeUp returns from Asleep to Idle. Stop and a DeviceReset that stays silent past the bound return Measuring to Idle. SoftReset, HardReset and Deinitialize return Idle to Uninitialized, and SoftReset or HardReset do the same from Measuring. A failed command in Idle or Measuring leaves the driver in StateUnknown, and EnsureInitialized returns it to Idle.

measurement-steps.title: Start, wait and read one measurement
measurement-steps.alt: One measurement with the SFM executor: StartMeasurement reads the scale factors and starts the sensor, your code sleeps the returned wait and polls, and ReadSample then reads nine bytes, checks each CRC and returns a sample.
measurement-steps.description: Participants, left to right: Your code, SfmFlowMeter<Port> and Your port. The steps run from top to bottom. Your code sends StartMeasurement(Air) to SfmFlowMeter<Port>. SfmFlowMeter<Port> sends Write(read-scale command) to Your port. Your port returns true to SfmFlowMeter<Port>. SfmFlowMeter<Port> sends Read(9 bytes: scale, offset, unit + CRC) to Your port. Your port returns true to SfmFlowMeter<Port>. A note over SfmFlowMeter<Port> says: CRC, compare with the table. SfmFlowMeter<Port> sends Write(start command) to Your port. SfmFlowMeter<Port> returns Result<Wait>{12 ms} to Your code. Your code does sleep 12 ms itself. Your code sends Poll() to SfmFlowMeter<Port>. SfmFlowMeter<Port> returns Result<Wait>{0} (measuring) to Your code. Your code sends ReadSample() to SfmFlowMeter<Port>. SfmFlowMeter<Port> sends Read(9 bytes) to Your port. A note over SfmFlowMeter<Port> says: CRC per word, status check, scale. SfmFlowMeter<Port> returns Result<Sample> to Your code.
